blocks.text: Grok 测试应用允许外部账户加入团队

inlines.text: Grok 测试应用允许外部账户加入团队

blocks.text: Claroc 自己的两个测试应用还暴露出另一个问题。一个联系人列表应用的数据库没有登录验证，匿名访客可以直接添加条目。在一个销售团队客户列表应用中，Grok 自行加入了 Google 和 X 登录。但在这个测试应用里，Grok 生成的代码先把每个通过身份验证的用户加入团队，之后才检查成员资格。于是一个外部 Google 账户就能读取、编辑和删除记录。Claroc 表示，写入和删除测试只在其自家应用上进行。

blocks.text: SpaceXSI 表示发布需要经过多个步骤

inlines.text: SpaceXSI 表示发布需要经过多个步骤

blocks.text: SpaceXSI 在回应此次披露时仅表示，应用在创建者分享之前都是私密的，发布需要经过多个步骤，包括一份法律声明，并且员工账号默认设为“仅限你”。Claroc 反驳称，如果最后一步仍然预选“任何拥有链接的人”，多几次点击也无济于事。该公司还表示，那 24 个开放的员工应用也说明，针对员工账号的更严格默认设置实际帮助甚微。

blocks.text: Claroc 建议 SpaceXSI 将“仅限你”设为默认，并在发布前显示谁将获得访问权限。Grok 还应在应用配有数据库却没有登录功能时发出警告。应用不应使用单独的子域名，而应运行在共享主机上难以猜测的路径下，这样其名称就不会出现在 DNS 数据中。

blocks.text: SpaceXSI 此后已将那 24 个员工应用下线，但尚未移除其他 Grok 用户和组织下的开放应用。Claroc 提出可以保密方式分享完整的地址列表。由于 SpaceXSI 未承诺联系受影响的拥有者，Claroc 现在直接通知他们。该公司在此事上也有自身利益，它销售针对 AI 构建应用的安全解决方案。

blocks.text: 这至少是 SpaceXSI 涉及 Grok 的第三起隐私事件。2025 年 8 月，Forbes 在 Google 搜索中发现超过 37 万条被分享的 Grok 对话。2026 年 7 月，终端工具 Grok Build 未经询问便将用户文件上传至公司服务器，其中包括 SSH 密钥和密码数据库。由于 Grok 生成色情深度伪造内容，爱尔兰数据保护机构也正在调查 X 是否忽视了设计层面的数据保护。

blocks.text: Apps built with the AI assistant Grok are almost always open to anyone with the link, according to a security firm. The exposed data includes patient records and confidential documents from Grok maker SpaceXSI itself.

inlines.text: Apps built with the AI assistant Grok are almost always open to anyone with the link, according to a security firm. The exposed data includes patient records and confidential documents from Grok maker SpaceXSI itself.

blocks.text: Security firm Claroc found more than 35,000 Grok-built apps that could be accessed without login, according to a recent report. In SpaceXSI's "Build" mode (the company was formerly xAI), users describe an app in a chat and Grok writes the code. An app only goes public when its creator clicks "Publish," which gives it its own address on grok.me.

blocks.text: Out of 37,571 apps Claroc checked that were still online, 35,578 were open to anyone. That's 94.7 percent, according to the report. Claroc points to the publish dialog as the cause. On the paid account the firm used for testing, "Anyone with the link" was already preselected. The addresses were also easy to find. Each app gets its own subdomain, so its name shows up in commercial passive DNS databases after the first visit. Those databases can be searched by pattern.

blocks.text: Grok test app let an outside account join the team

inlines.text: Grok test app let an outside account join the team

blocks.text: Two of Claroc's own test apps turned up another problem. A contact list app ended up with a database that had no login, so anonymous visitors could add entries. For a sales team customer list, Grok added Google and X sign-in on its own. In that test app, though, Grok's code added every authenticated user to the team first and only checked membership afterward. An outside Google account could then read, edit, and delete records. Claroc says it ran write and delete tests only on its own apps.

blocks.text: SpaceXSI says publishing takes several steps

inlines.text: SpaceXSI says publishing takes several steps

blocks.text: SpaceXSI responded to the disclosure only by saying that apps are private until their creator shares them, that publishing takes multiple steps including a legal notice, and that employee accounts default to "Only you." Claroc counters that extra clicks don't help if "Anyone with the link" is still preselected at the final step. The 24 open employee apps also show how little the stricter default for staff accounts actually helps, the firm says.

blocks.text: Claroc proposed that SpaceXSI make "Only you" the default and show who will have access before publishing. Grok should also warn when an app has a database but no login. Instead of individual subdomains, apps should run on hard-to-guess paths on a shared host so their names don't end up in DNS data.

blocks.text: SpaceXSI has since taken the 24 employee apps offline but hasn't removed the open apps from other Grok users and organizations. Claroc offered to share the full list of addresses confidentially. Because SpaceXSI didn't commit to contacting the affected owners, Claroc is now notifying them directly. The firm has its own interests here. It sells security solutions for AI-built apps.

blocks.text: This is at least the third privacy incident for SpaceXSI involving Grok. In August 2025, Forbes found more than 370,000 shared Grok conversations in Google Search. In July 2026, the terminal tool Grok Build uploaded user files to the company's servers without asking, including SSH keys and password databases. Because of sexualized deepfakes generated by Grok, Ireland's data protection authority is also investigating whether X neglected data protection by design.

found more than 370,000 shared Grok conversations in Google Search. In July 2026, the terminal tool Grok Build
uploaded user files to the company's servers without asking
, including SSH keys and password databases. Because of sexualized deepfakes generated by Grok, Ireland's data protection authority is also investigating whether X neglected
data protection by design
